templates.construct: Subtract a price from a bill to find the change

formats.prompt: Ana buys bread for {peso(price)} and pays with a {peso(bill)} bill. How much change should she get?

hints: Change is what is left of the {peso(bill)} after the {peso(price)} is taken out.
Count up instead of borrowing. From {price}, how many pesos reach the next ten?
That is {toTen} to reach {price + toTen}. Now count from {price + toTen} up to {bill}.

distractors.feedback: {peso(value)} is the bill and the price added together. Change is what is left once the price is taken away.
{peso(value)} is what the bread costs. The question asks what comes back from the {peso(bill)}.

templates.construct: Multiply a unit price by a quantity

formats.prompt: A sari-sari store sells {item} at {peso(each)} each. What do {n} cost?

hints: Same price {n} times over — that is multiplication.

distractors.feedback: {peso(value)} is the price of one. All {n} cost {n} × {peso(each)}.
{peso(value)} adds the price and the count. Each of the {n} costs {peso(each)}, so multiply.

templates.construct: Multiply a fare by a number of passengers

formats.prompt: A jeepney fare is {peso(fare)}. What do {riders} passengers pay?

hints: Each passenger pays the same fare, so this is {riders} lots of {fare}.
Round {fare} up to {fare + (10 - fare % 10)} if it helps, then take the extra back off.

distractors.feedback: {peso(value)} is the fare for one. The question asks what all {riders} pay together.
{peso(value)} adds the fare and the number of passengers. Each of the {riders} pays {peso(fare)}, so multiply.

templates.construct: Divide a total equally among people

formats.prompt: {people} friends share a {peso(total)} order equally. What does each one pay?

hints: Equal shares means dividing the total by {people}.
Halve it first if {people} is even — halving twice is dividing by four.
{total} ÷ {people} lands on a whole number of pesos here.

distractors.feedback: {peso(value)} is the whole bill. Each person pays only their share of it.
{peso(value)} multiplies by {people}. Sharing equally divides the total.

templates.construct: Subtract two purchases from a budget

formats.prompt: Mila has {peso(start)}. She spends {peso(a)} on rice and {peso(b)} on fish. How much is left?

hints: Two things came out of the same {peso(start)}.
Add the two amounts she spent before you subtract.

distractors.feedback: {peso(value)} takes away only the rice. Both purchases come out of the same money.
{peso(value)} is what she spent. The question asks what is left of the {peso(start)}.
{peso(value)} takes the rice away but adds the fish back on. Both purchases come out of the same money.
